add_comment.description: Pin feedback to passages without changing them, for reviews and critique. Every point goes in this one call, in document order; the user sees each as a card at its passage, so your reply is a short overall summary.

comments.description: One per point (each word, when glossing words)

anchor.description: Only for a few words inside the block: those words, verbatim. Left out, the whole block.

comment.description: Specific, actionable feedback, in the user's language

suggestion.description: Only for a concrete rewrite: the anchor (or the whole block) as it should read, in markdown, which the user applies with one click. Left out where the writer must judge.

check_conventions.description: Check the document's writing conventions with a rules engine - punctuation and spacing (full-width CJK marks, French no-break spaces, quotes, dashes, ellipses), numbers and dates, spelling lists, consistency - under the profile in force: the whole document, a section by `heading`, a line range, or a draft `text`. Returns findings by rule, each with its line, text, fix and why; changes nothing.

heading.description: Part of the section's heading; wins over a line range

strict.description: Also style hints: long sentences, wordiness, passive voice

text.description: A draft (markdown) to check against the document's conventions

edit_file.description: Change part of a file in the folder: `old`, verbatim and found once in it (read_file it first), becomes `new`. One call per change. Not for the open document: propose_edit changes that.

new.description: What it becomes; empty deletes it

old.description: The text to replace, verbatim, enough to be unique

find_files.description: Find files in the project folder by name: text files, and PDF, Word, PowerPoint, spreadsheet, EPUB and RTF files (case-insensitive; every word must be in the path, so "chapter 3" finds drafts/chapter-3.md), documents first. Without `name`, lists every file.

name.description: Part of the file's name or path

find_files+images.description: Find files in the project folder by name: text files, PDF, Word, PowerPoint, spreadsheet, EPUB and RTF files, and images, marked "(image)" (case-insensitive; every word must be in the path, so "chapter 3" finds drafts/chapter-3.md), documents first. Without `name`, lists every file.

name.description: Part of the file's name or path

measure_text.description: Count text exactly for a length limit; never estimate a count yourself. Limits: x_weighted 280 (URLs 23, CJK and emoji 2), bluesky 300 graphemes, threads 500, instagram 2,200 (at most 5 hashtags), mastodon 500, linkedin 3,000 (fold near 140), wechat_title 32, wechat_digest 120, xhs_title 20, xhs_body 1,000, govuk_title 65, govuk_summary 160, zh_academic_title 25 字; without `metric`, the basic counts. Not for a length the user asks for: write that straight into propose_edit, whose result gives its size.

text.description: The exact text, as it will be used

propose_edit.description: Propose edits to the document; each lands as the user set it: a revision to accept or reject, or written straight in. Send every edit of the reply in this one call, in document order. Each block (paragraph, heading, whole list, quote, table, code block or picture) starts with its id, like `[#k3f9]`, which is never part of `text` or `anchor`. With `block` alone, `replace` swaps the block for `text`, `delete` removes it, and `insert_before`/`insert_after` add `text` as a new block beside it. With an `anchor` (found once in the block; quote more if it repeats), `replace` and `delete` act on it, and `insert_before`/`insert_after` add `text` beside it: within the paragraph when it is a phrase or sentence (after the last sentence, continuing the paragraph); as a new block when `text` is block content; as a new line of the table or list when it is a whole row or item line - how rows and items are added, `text` being only the new line(s), nested items keeping their indentation. `replace_selection` replaces the <selected-text>, `insert_at_cursor` adds `text` at the <cursor> (only when the message has one), and `append` adds it at the end; none takes an `anchor`. `last_block` extends one replace through consecutive blocks; the user still decides on each paragraph. Pictures in that run stay in `text` unchanged: a text edit never changes a picture; `delete` by its block removes one.

anchor.description: The few words in the block the edit is about, verbatim; left out, the whole block. Without `block` (only for undecided text you proposed, which has no id): that text, verbatim.

block.description: The target block's id, `k3f9` for `[#k3f9]`. Write it first.

last_block.description: Only for one replace of consecutive blocks: the last one's id

reason.description: Why, in one short sentence in your reply's language, shown on the proposal card ("Cut the repeated point about cost")

text.description: The new content, in markdown; for every action but `delete`

read_document.description: Read part of the document verbatim, before revising a passage you can't see in full: a section by its heading, subsections included, or a range of lines from the outline. Blocks come back after their `[#id]`.

heading.description: Part of the section's heading; wins over a line range

start_line.description: First line, 1-based, as in the outline and search results

read_file.description: Read a file of the project folder by the path find_files or search_files shows: a text file, or a PDF, Word, PowerPoint, spreadsheet, EPUB or RTF file as Markdown. A long file comes in parts, and the answer says which lines it shows; start_line and end_line read a part, such as a few dozen lines around a search_files match.

path.description: Path relative to the project folder

start_line.description: First line, 1-based, as in search_files results

read_file+images.description: Read a file of the project folder by the path find_files or search_files shows: a text file, or a PDF, Word, PowerPoint, spreadsheet, EPUB or RTF file as Markdown - or look at an image (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, up to 6 MB: a map, a photo, a chart, a scan). A long file comes in parts, and the answer says which lines it shows; start_line and end_line read a part, such as a few dozen lines around a search_files match.

path.description: Path relative to the project folder

start_line.description: First line, 1-based, as in search_files results

search_conversations.description: Search the user's earlier conversations with you, about every document, newest first, when they refer to something said before that isn't in this conversation or in what you remember ("the title we chose last time"). Every word must be in one message or reply: search for a word or two it would contain, in its language. Returns the passages with their conversation's title and date.

query.description: A word or two that would be in what was said

search_document.description: Search the document for a word or phrase (case-insensitive): each matching line, with its number and its block's id.

search_files.description: Search every text file and document (PDF, Word, PowerPoint, spreadsheet, EPUB, RTF) in the project folder for a word or phrase (case-insensitive), however long the file, to find where a character, term or fact appears. Returns `path:line: text` matches; read_file around one for its context.

search_references.description: Search the user's reference library - the papers, books, reports and notes in the project's `{}/` folder - for the passages that best answer a question, best first. Pass the words the sources would use; several are fine. Each result is `path:first-last` and the passage: cite the source by its file name, and read_file around it for more. For research in the references, prefer it to search_files, which finds one exact phrase anywhere.

query.description: What the passages should be about, in the sources' own words

use_skill.description: Load a skill's full instructions (from the list in the system prompt, or app-guide), or a reference pack a skill names. Call it before following a skill whose description the request matches, or that the user names.

name.description: The skill's name as listed, or a pack such as standards-fr or standards-fr#dialogue

write_file.description: Create a file in the folder, or replace one's whole text; for a few changes to one, edit_file is safer. Not for the open document: propose_edit changes that. Changing several files: first say in a line or two which and how, then make the changes without waiting for an answer.

path.description: The file, from the folder, e.g. `chapters/03.md`; folders are made as needed
